subject: Quantamed: private/VPC deployment security intake and next steps
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@quantamed.com>, Lydia Cho <lydia.cho@quantamed.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Quantamed private deployment: quick post-call recap & questionnaire kickoff

Hi Evan / Lydia —

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clarity on QuantaMed's isolation requirements and the use cases that will drive latency constraints (real-time summarization for clinician notes). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- SOC 2 / compliance: You asked what evidence Redwood can share. We have a SOC 2 Type II attestation and a HIPAA BA template. I’ve attached a stub pointing to the attestation link and the BA workflow.
- Deployment modes: you flagged two options — (1) VPC private deployment (customer VPC peering or transit), and (2) fully air-gapped on-prem. We can support both; air-gapped engagements require a short professional services scope for install+validation.
- Network ask: please send your network diagram (site-to-site, IP ranges, NAT/failover policy) and preferred control-plane connectivity (outbound only vs. dedicated management link).
- Vendor questionnaire: I attached the questionnaire (Quantamed_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf). If you can return the completed PDF, we’ll triage answers and flag any follow-ups.

Immediate proposed next steps: 
1) Evan/Lydia to complete questionnaire + upload network diagram by EOW 7/18.
2) Redwood (Neha + Aditya) to produce an internal reference architecture sketch and list of required ports, firewall rules, and KMS integration notes (deliverable: redwood_onprem_reference_sketch_v1.pdf). Target: 7/14.
3) If you prefer, schedule a 30-min technical follow-up to walk the diagram and any HIPAA evidence requirements — we’re free 7/15-7/17.

Attachments: Quantamed_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf (fillable), SOC2_Attestation_Link.txt (link), network_diagram_sketch.png (example placeholder)

Thanks — I’ll loop back with the reference sketch tomorrow.

—
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0179

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@quantamed.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Lydia Cho <lydia.cho@quantamed.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantamed private deployment: quick post-call recap & questionnaire kickoff

Chloe — thanks for the crisp summary. Quick replies inline: 

- Questionnaire: I’ll start on this today. Expect the filled PDF by 7/18 as you suggested.
- Network diagram: attaching our current on-prem sketch (coming from our infra team) — it’s rough, but shows our DMZ, clinician VLANs, and the segmented research cluster.
- Air-gapped engagement: good to know about PS for install. Can you share rough range for the engagement length/cost or a checklist of what's required? That’ll help me triage internally.

Two clarifying Qs: 
1) For the private VPC option, do you require a persistent control-plane connection, or can the control plane be run via outbound-only egress with mutual TLS?
2) For HIPAA BA: do you require any additional attestation other than a signed BA + SOC 2 report (e.g., penetration test report)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Evan

--
Evan Brooks
Head of IT Infrastructure
QuantaMed
evan.brooks@quantamed.com
(617) 555-4310

Attachment: quantamed_onprem_sketch_v0.png

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@quantamed.com>, Lydia Cho <lydia.cho@quantamed.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 09:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantamed private deployment: quick post-call recap & questionnaire kickoff

Evan — appreciate the fast response and the sketch. A few concrete answers to your questions: 

- Control plane connectivity: Outbound-only with mutual TLS is our preferred model for Private (no inbound firewall changes required). That said, we can support dedicated management links for higher-assurance setups; we’ll map that in the reference sketch.
- HIPAA evidence: Signed BA + SOC 2 Type II cover most customers. For clinical/regulatory programs, some customers request a recent penetration test or a summary of remediation. If QuantaMed requires full pentest artifacts we can discuss scoping (PS + legal review).
- Air-gapped PS scope: Typical engagements run 2–4 weeks on-site (depending on hardware readiness). The checklist we’ll deliver tomorrow includes: staging VM images, hardware/network prerequisites, signed project statement, and acceptance tests.

Neha and Aditya — attaching the reference sketch we discussed (redwood_onprem_reference_sketch_v1.pdf). It includes: required ports (outbound 443 with mTLS to control endpoints), optional NTP/DNS allowances, KMS handshake notes, and a short fallback plan (model-variant routing to hosted fallback during maintenance).

Evan/Lydia — if you can highlight spots in your sketch where the public control endpoints would be routable (or mark them as egress-only), we’ll overlay our IP ranges and finalize the diagram.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_reference_sketch_v1.pdf, SOC2_Attestation_Link.txt

Best,
Chloe

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@quantamed.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantamed private deployment: quick post-call recap & questionnaire kickoff

Hi all — adding a couple of brief technical notes from an infra perspective: 

- Latency: for clinician-facing summarization we recommend provisioning for p95 response targets in the reference sketch; this affects instance sizing more than network topology. If you share expected concurrency we can right-size GPU pools.
- KV/cache and model fallbacks: in private deployments we can configure a local KV cache for prefix reuse; if you want an air-gapped split with occasional hosted fallback, we recommend an explicit routing policy and read-only token for the fallback path.
- Ports/Protocol: main egress is 443 mTLS. For telemetry/observability during onboarding we ask for a temporary outbound to our collection endpoints — this can be revoked post onboarding.

I’ve attached a minimal-ops diagram and a short checklist (redwood_onprem_reference_sketch_v1.pdf). Happy to walk this in the follow-up call.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Lydia Cho <lydia.cho@quantamed.com>

Subject: Re: Quantamed private deployment: quick post-call recap & questionnaire kickoff

Thanks Chloe / Aditya — this is exactly what we needed. A couple of quick notes from our side: 

- Timeline: we’ll aim to return the completed questionnaire and a marked-up network diagram by COB 7/18.
- HIPAA: for our legal review we will request signed BA + SOC 2 Type II first; if legal asks for pentest details we’ll circle back.
- Air-gap: we’re leaning toward VPC-private first, with an evaluation for air-gapped for Tier 1 patient data workloads later this year. Please include a short addendum in the PS checklist with estimated on-site days and any hardware/firmware constraints.

Let’s tentatively hold 7/16 11:00–11:30 PT for a technical walkthrough — Evan will confirm with infra.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
